title: Microsoft Purview eDiscovery: customer-managed keys for direct export (GCC, GCC High, DoD)
summary: Hold: the Customer Key licensing guidance omits the tenant-wide licence-count requirement for multi-workload encryption, including the consequence that insufficient licences cause encryption to revert. The roadmap details, support-request enablement and policy-assignment command are supported.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans customer-managed key options for eDiscovery direct export, adding to existing Microsoft-managed encryption.
claims.quote: allowing users to manage their own encryption keys for the data included in the direct export workflow in eDiscovery, adding to the Microsoft-managed encryption already in place.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance; rationale: risk
claims.claim: This protection covers direct exports, not data at rest in eDiscovery review sets.

claims.where: Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The tenant must remain CMK enabled at export time.
claims.quote: Your tenant must remain CMK enabled at the time of the export.

claims.claim: The export documentation does not explain export behaviour when the tenant is not CMK enabled.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery CMK export enabled status. Read purview/edisc-search-export and searched the eDiscovery API guide for CMK and encryption; no fallback behaviour stated.

claims.claim: Search export packages expire 14 days after export creation; this is a general search-export rule.
claims.quote: Search export packages expire 14 days after you create the export. ... This expiry applies only to search exports, not to review set exports.

claims.claim: Expired search exports and their package data are automatically deleted and cannot be recovered.
claims.quote: After 14 days, the export and all data contained in the export package are automatically deleted and can't be recovered.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Learn describes no additional CMK step for the exporting user.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery CMK direct export enable PowerShell Graph API portal setting; eDiscovery CMK export enabled status. Read the CMK prerequisites and full export procedure in purview/edisc-search-export; no exporting-user CMK step.

claims.claim: Customer Key onboarding for GCC High and DoD requires contacting Microsoft Support for US Government onboarding.
claims.quote: For GCC-H and DoD tenants, contact Microsoft Support and request onboarding for U.S. government tenants.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Customer Key licensing requirements
claims.claim: The Customer Key licensing requirement is presented as a licence for each benefiting user without the workload-specific tenant licence-count qualification.
claims.quote: your tenant must have at least as many Customer Key licenses as users assigned Exchange or Teams licenses—whichever is greater. ... If your tenant doesn't have enough eligible licenses, encryption reverts to the default service encryption.
claims.fix: After 'each user who benefits from Customer Key requires a licence', add: 'For Customer Key for Multiple Workloads, the tenant must have at least as many Customer Key licences as users assigned Exchange or Teams licences, whichever is greater. SharePoint is licensed separately and excluded from that count. Microsoft periodically validates the count; insufficient eligible licences cause encryption to revert to default service encryption.' Keep the existing service-description citation.

claims.quote: Microsoft 365 E5/A5/G5, Microsoft Purview Suite/EDU/GOV/FLW, Microsoft 365 E5/A5/F5/G5 Information Protection and Governance | Office 365 E5/A5/G5; Customer Key | Included | Included

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The export page requires an eDiscovery user to have a Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3 or E5 licence.
claims.quote: To export content in eDiscovery, assign the eDiscovery user a Microsoft 365 Enterprise E3 or E5 license.

claims.claim: The account also needs a Microsoft SharePoint E3 licence when exporting SharePoint content; this is not CMK-specific.
claims.quote: When exporting SharePoint content, the account must also have a Microsoft SharePoint E3 license; otherwise, SharePoint items might not export as expected.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; front matter: licensing.notes
claims.claim: No licence specific to CMK direct export is named beyond the documented Customer Key and export requirements.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery CMK licensing direct. Read edisc-search-export, customer-key-set-up and the Customer Key service-description section; results describe Customer Key and eDiscovery licensing, not a separate CMK-direct-export licence.

claims.claim: Learn publishes no separate charge specifically for CMK on direct export.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery CMK direct export licensing charge. Read edisc-search-export, edisc-billing and Customer Key licensing/setup. Billing documents data-storage and E3 export-API charges, but no separate CMK encryption charge.

claims.claim: The export page's CMK section does not specify government-cloud applicability or a distinct government enablement route.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery CMK direct export enable licensing charge GCC DEP type. Read edisc-search-export: government endpoints appear in download guidance, but the CMK section gives no government-specific applicability or request route.

claims.claim: The service description's Customer Key section does not explain how its licensing applies to government clouds.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery CMK direct export licensing charge GCC. Searched the service description for Customer Key, GCC and government; the Customer Key section lists G5 plans but no cloud-specific interpretation.

claims.claim: The GCC High planning page lists Customer Key data-at-rest encryption for Microsoft 365 as Available.
claims.quote: Customer Key: Data-at-rest encryption for Microsoft 365 | Available

claims.claim: The GCC planning page lists Customer Key data-at-rest encryption for Microsoft 365 as Available.
claims.quote: Customer Key: Data-at-rest encryption for Microsoft 365 | Available

claims.claim: The cited GCC and GCC High planning pages do not mention CMK for eDiscovery direct export.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery CMK direct export GCC. Read both cited Purview GCC and GCC High deployment pages in full; their tables list general Customer Key and export availability, not CMK direct export.

claims.claim: No administrator UI switch or API for enabling CMK direct export is documented; enablement uses a support request.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery CMK direct export enable PowerShell Graph API portal setting; eDiscovery CMK direct exports PowerShell Graph. Read edisc-search-export and searched edisc-ref-api-guide for CMK/customer/encryption; no enablement operation.

claims.claim: No administrator portal path for assigning the multi-workload DEP is documented.
claims.quote: Searched: Customer Key assign multi-workload data encryption policy admin portal UI PolicyAssigned. Read customer-key-manage and customer-key-set-up; assignment uses Exchange Online PowerShell, not a portal path.

claims.where: controls[1].api; rendered controls table; Governance controls; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Set-M365DataAtRestEncryptionPolicyAssignment -DataEncryptionPolicy <PolicyName or ID> assigns the multi-workload DEP and is not a status check.
claims.quote: After creating a multi-workload data encryption policy (DEP), assign it using the Set-M365DataAtRestEncryptionPolicyAssignment cmdlet. ... Set-M365DataAtRestEncryptionPolicyAssignment -DataEncryptionPolicy <PolicyName or ID>

claims.claim: The Customer Key manage page requires Exchange admin permissions and describes DEP operations as using Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Permissions: Exchange admin permissions (all DEP operations run through Exchange Online PowerShell)

claims.where: controls[1].note; Governance controls; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The export page does not explicitly name the DEP type as multi-workload, Exchange-mailbox or SharePoint.
claims.quote: Searched: eDiscovery CMK direct export DEP type; Customer Key assign multi-workload data encryption policy PolicyAssigned. Read edisc-search-export: it specifies MDEP and PolicyAssigned, but does not explicitly label one of the three DEP types.

claims.claim: DEP assignment is an administrator-run prerequisite rather than the switch enabling the feature, described misleadingly as the only administrator-run control.
claims.quote: After setting up Customer Key, create and assign one or more data encryption policies (DEPs) ... For example, you can verify encryption status, view DEP details, disable a DEP, restore keys, or roll back to Microsoft-managed keys.
claims.fix: Replace 'The only control an administrator runs is the DEP assignment, which is a prerequisite for the feature, not a setting on it' with 'DEP assignment is a prerequisite for the feature, not its enablement setting.'

claims.claim: The policy-assignment cmdlet changes the policy at tenant scope.
claims.quote: Use the Set-M365DataAtRestEncryptionPolicyAssignment cmdlet to assign a Microsoft 365 data-at-rest encryption policy at the tenant level.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout, DEP confirmation bullet
claims.claim: The checklist directs readers to confirm DEP status using a controls row that provides only assignment, not verification.
claims.quote: Confirm that Customer Key is configured and that your DEP is in PolicyAssigned state, using the Customer Key controls row below. / It assigns the policy, so do not use it as a status check.
claims.fix: Remove 'using the Customer Key controls row below' from the confirmation bullet. Keep its warning that the assignment cmdlet is not a status check; the checklist's verification step has no corresponding verification control row.

controlChecks.governs: The data encryption policy assigned to the tenant, a prerequisite for CMK direct export
